judgments.reason: The bound resource description explicitly names a schematic example substance and the alt text excludes a universal rule for all solids or a claim of measured data. The unnumbered schematic does not establish real numerical values. A positive-slope example does not require depicting every possible substance/evaporation scenario. Subsequent instruction must retain this existing condition; no universal temperature law is approved.

The faceted pale solids could resemble ice if detached from context. Here they settle at the bottom beneath a substantial still-liquid layer, while the current goal/resource explicitly describes dissolved solid crystallisation. There is no ice/snow label, no subzero numerical scale and no assertion that the solvent froze. In the actual bound teaching context they function as deposited solute crystals rather than bulk frozen water.

Both vessels are covered, have comparable liquid levels and show no outgoing vapour, water loss or empty cooled vessel. This is compatible with the stated no-water-loss cooling example. Schematic equal liquid level does not assert exact solution-volume conservation or a measured solvent balance.

Warm/cold labels, cooling arrow, clear versus crystal-containing vessel and both graph-axis words remain readable at360 and680. Thermometer colours support thermal contrast without relying on tiny scale readings. No clipping or contradictory flow direction observed.
